events.name: Festival de la Médina de Tunis
events.text: Evening concerts of traditional and tarab music, theatre and workshops held during Ramadan in the old town of Tunis and venues such as the Théâtre Municipal; the 42nd edition took place in 2026. Dates follow Ramadan and move about eleven days earlier each year.

events.name: International Festival of the Saharan Ksour
events.text: Spring festival of southern Berber heritage, founded in 1979, with folk shows, horsemanship displays and a crafts fair around the region's fortified granaries. It has been irregular recently: after the 2022 edition it paused, and regional authorities announced a revival for March 2026.

events.name: Ghriba Pilgrimage (Lag BaOmer)
events.text: Annual Jewish pilgrimage to the El Ghriba synagogue in Er-Riadh, on Djerba, around Lag BaOmer, with prayers and processions. Attendance has fallen since a 2023 attack, and the 2026 pilgrimage went ahead under tight security.

events.name: Falconry Festival (Festival de l'Épervier)
events.text: Three-day festival on Cap Bon where local falconers show and compete with trained sparrowhawks and peregrine falcons, alongside exhibitions and talks. Held each June; 2025 was the 56th edition.

events.name: Tabarka Jazz Festival
events.text: Jazz festival on the north coast, founded in 1973, now also featuring world and contemporary music, with free street jazz in the evenings. It returned in July 2026 at the open-air Théâtre de la Mer after a six-year break, so it is not held every year.

events.name: International Festival of Dougga
events.text: Summer concerts in the Roman theatre of the Dougga archaeological site, with a programme weighted toward Tunisian artists. Held most summers; the 50th edition ran over ten evenings in July 2026.

events.name: International Malouf Festival of Testour
events.text: Week-long festival of malouf (Tunisian Arab-Andalusian music) and traditional Arab music in the Andalusian town of Testour, founded in 1967. Usually held in July, but the 2026 edition was cancelled.

events.name: Aoussou Carnival
events.text: Sousse's summer carnival, with a parade of floats, brass bands and folk troupes from Tunisia and abroad, traditionally on 24 July near Boujaafar beach. Held most years (cancelled in 2014, resumed in 2015).

events.name: International Festival of Carthage
events.text: Tunisia's best-known summer festival, held every July and August since 1964 in the restored Roman theatre of Carthage. Mainly concerts by Arab and international artists, plus some theatre and dance.

events.name: Hammamet International Festival
events.text: Annual summer festival of music and performing arts, running since 1964 in a 1,000-seat open-air amphitheatre overlooking the Gulf of Hammamet. Evenings of concerts and shows through July and August.

events.name: El Jem International Festival of Symphonic Music
events.text: Orchestras from Tunisia and abroad perform classical concerts inside the third-century Roman amphitheatre of El Jem. Held every summer since the mid-1980s, with concerts spread over July and August.

events.name: Sfax International Festival
events.text: Summer programme of concerts, stage shows and screenings at Sfax's open-air theatre, featuring Tunisian and Arab stars. Held yearly from late July to mid-August; 2026 was the 46th edition.

events.name: Kerkennah Festival
events.text: Popular summer festival on the Kerkennah islands off Sfax, with music, comedy, rap and children's shows. The 30th edition ran from late July to early August 2025.

events.name: Mouled (Mawlid) in Kairouan
events.text: Kairouan, Tunisia's spiritual capital, draws hundreds of thousands of visitors for the Prophet's birthday, with free shows and sound-and-light displays over about a week. The date follows the Islamic calendar: early September in 2025, late August in 2026, moving earlier each year.

events.name: Carthage Theatre Days (JTC)
events.text: Theatre festival created in 1983, with more than 80 shows from Tunisia, the Arab world and Africa and a competition for the Tanit awards, centred on the Cité de la Culture in Tunis. Recent editions have been annual, in late November.

events.name: Carthage Film Festival (JCC)
events.text: Film festival founded in 1966 and annual since 2014, screening African and Arab cinema in Tunis and awarding the Tanit d'or. Traditionally in October–November; recent editions have run in December.

events.name: International Festival of the Sahara
events.text: Four-day festival of desert life held each year at the end of December in Douz, gateway to the Sahara. Expect camel races, fantasia horsemanship, a Bedouin wedding, poetry and music, mostly at the H'naiech stadium on the edge of the dunes.

events.name: International Festival of the Oases
events.text: Late-December festival, first held in 1938, celebrating the Jerid's oases and the date harvest with evening concerts, fantasia, street arts and craft and date markets across Tozeur. Held most years.
